packageRules.description: Auto-merge non-breaking updates, whatever manager they come from. A minor or patch bump whose tests pass is the case this exists for; leaving it open is how a repository ends up eight releases behind. Restricting this to gomod left every npm, pip and container bump sitting green and unmerged.

Never auto-merge the Go toolchain. A library that breaks is one library; a toolchain that breaks is every architecture at once, and the failure is not in the change but somewhere else, later, in code nobody touched. One is broken today: go1.27.0 miscompiles on loong64 (golang/go#81000, bisected on real hardware to 3fdac6780b), and go-gfx/gfx fails its loong64 lane on exactly that bump while its other ten pass. A repository without a loong64 lane sees nothing. The bump is still proposed, and a person still looks at it.
